NHTSA lists these five recalls for the 2020 Honda Civic:

| Campaign # | Component | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| **21V215000** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The in-tank low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine while driving. It expands recall 20V-314. |
| **23V458000** | Service brakes: master cylinder | An improperly assembled tie rod fastener can let the brake master cylinder separate from the booster, causing loss of braking. |
| **23V858000** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The in-tank fuel pump can fail and stall the engine. It expands 21V-215 and 20V-314 across many models. |
| **24V064000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | The passenger seat weight sensor can crack and short-circuit, so the airbag may not be suppressed as intended. |
| **26V332000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | The same cracked sensor can cause the airbags to deploy unintentionally in a crash. It expands 24V064. |

- **Accuracy:** I pulled this from NHTSA's recalls API, and a summarizing tool condensed the results. Check the campaign numbers and wording against nhtsa.gov/recalls before you rely on them.
- **Not every Civic is covered:** Recalls often apply only to certain trims, builds or production ranges. Enter the specific car's VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or ask a Honda dealer to run it. That also shows whether the repairs were already done.
- **Open recalls:** Honda dealers do the repairs free. Before you buy, confirm that any open recalls are completed or will be fixed as part of the sale. The fuel pump and brake master cylinder recalls matter most, since they affect driving safety.

In 2025 Stripe shipped two GA API versions with breaking changes: `2025-03-31.basil` and `2025-09-30.clover`. Every other GA version that year (Acacia in January and February, Basil from April to August, Clover from October to December) is marked non-breaking. The rest of the breaking entries are on the opt-in `.preview` versions, which I list separately below.

I pulled this from Stripe's per-release changelog pages and each entry's "Breaking change?" column. I summarized the entries from their titles in the changelog tables, not from each entry's detail page. Check the linked page for exact field names before you upgrade.

## `2025-03-31.basil` (March 31, 2025)

**Billing**
- Subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed. Billing periods now live on subscription items.
- Invoicing resources get a `parent` field saying how they were generated.
- Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items replace their top-level price fields with a new price model.
- Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items replace their top-level tax properties with a new tax model.
- Invoices support multiple (partial) payments, which changes the payment-related fields.
- Coupons without an end time are no longer supported.
- The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts.
- The Upcoming Invoice API methods are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
- Legacy usage-based billing is removed.

**Checkout**
- Checkout Session no longer has `shipping_details`.
- Subscription Checkout Sessions now create the subscription only after the customer pays, with new update semantics.

**Payments**
- The manual capture method is removed for Interac cards.
- Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after creation.
- Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
- The Vault and Forward API returns 402 on upstream request timeouts.

**Issuing**
- There is a new reason code for authorizations created while Stripe is unavailable.
- Webhooks for Issuing authorizations now send an `Accept: application/json` header.
- Authorizations get a new `expired` status.

**Connect and other**
- `total_count` can no longer be expanded on list endpoints, across all products.
- There are new error codes for required verifications.
- The Person political-exposure property changes from a string to an enum.
- The Payment Element has a new default layout (Stripe.js).

## `2025-09-30.clover` (September 30, 2025)

**Billing**
- Subscription schedules lose the `iterations` parameter.
- Promotion Codes now reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
- Discount gets a `source` property and loses its `coupon` property.
- Flexible billing mode becomes the default for new subscriptions.
- Schedule phase end dates now account for billing cycle anchor changes.

**Checkout and Elements (Stripe.js)**
- Postal code is removed for card payments in certain regions.
- The currency conversion field is removed from Checkout Sessions.
- `redirectToCheckout` is removed.
- `initCheckout` becomes synchronous.
- The default for saved payment methods in Elements with Checkout Sessions changes.
- Client secrets for Intents in certain states can't be reused when initializing Elements.
- The deprecated messaging and bank Elements are removed.

**Payments, Radar and Issuing**
- The decline codes change for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and South Korean payment methods.
- Submitted stablecoin payments get a `processing` status.
- Radar manual reviews get new enum values.
- Issuing Authorization risk levels move to standard values.

**Connect**
- There are more specific descriptions for risk requirements during legal, PEP and sanctions review.
- There is a new error code for business type validations.

## Preview-channel breaking changes in 2025

These apply only if you pin a `.preview` version. They mostly cover Accounts v2, money management and Billing previews.

| Version | Breaking change |
|---|---|
| 2025-04-30.preview | Payouts become a capability (Accounts v2) |
| 2025-05-28.preview | Tax association status fields are replaced |
| 2025-05-28.preview | The Payment Intent field linking a tax calculation is renamed |
| 2025-06-30.preview | Billing mode configuration is consolidated into one hash |
| 2025-07-30.preview | Account Links v2 is enabled for Accounts v2 |
| 2025-07-30.preview | The Balance Settings custom settlement timing parameter is renamed |
| 2025-07-30.preview | Weekly and monthly payout schedule customization is updated |
| 2025-07-30.preview | Payment review closed reasons get a new value |
| 2025-08-27.preview | Flexible billing mode is the default for new subscriptions |
| 2025-08-27.preview | The `iterations` parameter is removed from schedule phases |
| 2025-08-27.preview | The Balance Settings request object is nested under `payments` |
| 2025-09-30.preview | Aggregated Billing meter usage data gets pagination and field updates |
| 2025-09-30.preview | Platform-specific identity fields move to a default profile for Accounts |
| 2025-09-30.preview | The Smart Disputes recommended evidence field is restructured |
| 2025-10-29.preview | There is a new error code for missing verification data on connected accounts |
| 2025-10-29.preview | Accounts v2 payment method billing details can be used for Stripe Tax location |
| 2025-11-17.preview | Accounts v2 requirements collection parameters are updated |
| 2025-11-17.preview | Accounts v2 gets a future requirements field |
| 2025-11-17.preview | There are health alerts for events that fail to generate |
| 2025-11-17.preview | Meter Usage Analytics can filter multiple tenants and dimension values |
| 2025-12-15.preview | Accounts v2 always returns `responsibilities` when `defaults` is included |
| 2025-12-15.preview | `requested` is removed from Accounts v2 capabilities hashes |
| 2025-12-15.preview | Payout Methods get generic error types |

For your pinned version, going to Basil means the big billing and invoice remodel. Going to Clover on top of that mostly affects subscription schedules, discounts and coupons, and Stripe.js Checkout and Elements.

Sources:
- [Stripe changelog: Basil](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil)
- [Stripe changelog: Clover](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover)
- [Stripe changelog: Acacia](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/acacia)
- [Stripe changelog (main)](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog)

Here are 8 well-known services. Most figures come from vendor pages and third-party comparison sites, and two come from my own knowledge, as noted. Free tiers change often, so check each vendor's pricing page before you commit.

| Service | Free monitors | Shortest interval | Free alert channels |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UptimeRobot** | 50 | 5 min | Email. One source says SMS and voice come from a one-time credit bundle, but its own table says 0 SMS credits. |
| **Better Stack** | 10 monitors plus 10 heartbeats | 3 min | Email and Slack. |
| **StatusCake** | 10 uptime monitors, plus 1 SSL, 1 domain and 1 page-speed monitor | 5 min | Email, plus integrations such as Slack, Discord and Telegram. |
| **HetrixTools** | 15 | 1 min | Email, plus integrations (Slack, Discord, Telegram, PagerDuty, webhooks) according to one comparison. A 2023 blog also mentions SMS. |
| **Site24x7** | Up to 50 resources | Not stated for the free plan | Email only. |
| **Hyperping** | 20 | 5 min | Email. |
| **Pulsetic** | 10 | 3 min | Email. |
| **Uptime Kuma** (self-hosted, open source) | Unlimited, limited by your server | About 20 sec, from memory | Many channels, such as email, Slack, Telegram, Discord and webhooks, from memory. |

**Caveats**
- **UptimeRobot:** The free plan is for non-commercial use only. StatusCake's free plan allows business use.
- **Hyperping:** A third-party tracker says the cap rose from 5 to 20 monitors in April 2026, while the interval slowed from 3 to 5 minutes.
- **Pulsetic:** The only source for these figures is Hyperping's comparison table, and I found no independent confirmation.
- **HetrixTools:** The 15-monitor and 1-minute figures are consistent across sources, but I didn't reach its official pricing page (it returned a 403). The alert channels come from third-party comparisons.
- **Site24x7:** The page I read didn't state an interval for the free plan.
- **Pingdom:** I left it out because it appears to have no free plan. One competitor guide says it now starts at $15/month.
- **Freshping:** I left it out because one guide says Freshworks shut it down on March 6, 2026. Other listings still show the old 50 monitors at 1 minute, but they look outdated.

**Quick take**
- **Most monitors:** UptimeRobot and Site24x7 (50 each).
- **Fastest checks:** HetrixTools (1 min).
- **Business use:** StatusCake, HetrixTools and Better Stack are the better fits, but Better Stack's pricing page labels its free tier for personal projects. Check the terms of the others.

As of October 2026, about 20 states have a comprehensive privacy law already in effect, and a few more have enacted one that takes effect later. The dates come from a web search plus my own knowledge. Trackers disagree on some details, so check a primary source such as the IAPP tracker before relying on a date for compliance.

**In effect**

| State | Law | Effective |
|---|---|---|
| California | Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), amended by the CPRA | Jan 1, 2020 (CPRA amendments Jan 1, 2023) |
| Virginia | Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA) | Jan 1, 2023 |
| Colorado | Colorado Privacy Act (CPA) | Jul 1, 2023 |
| Connecticut | Connecticut Data Privacy Act (CTDPA) | Jul 1, 2023 |
| Utah | Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA) | Dec 31, 2023 |
| Texas | Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA) | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Oregon | Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (OCPA) | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Florida | Digital Bill of Rights | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Montana | Consumer Data Privacy Act (MCDPA) | Oct 1, 2024 |
| Delaware | Personal Data Privacy Act (DPDPA) | Jan 1, 2025 |
| Iowa | Consumer Data Protection Act (ICDPA) | Jan 1, 2025 |
| Nebraska | Data Privacy Act (NDPA) | Jan 1, 2025 |
| New Hampshire | Privacy Act (NHPA) | Jan 1, 2025 |
| New Jersey | Data Privacy Act (NJDPA) | Jan 15, 2025 |
| Tennessee | Information Protection Act (TIPA) | Jul 1, 2025 |
| Minnesota | Consumer Data Privacy Act (MCDPA) | Jul 31, 2025 |
| Maryland | Online Data Privacy Act (MODPA) | Oct 1, 2025, but it applies to processing from Apr 1, 2026 |
| Indiana | Consumer Data Protection Act | Jan 1, 2026 |
| Kentucky | Consumer Data Protection Act | Jan 1, 2026 |
| Rhode Island | Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act | Jan 1, 2026 |

**Enacted, not yet in effect (less certain; the search results were thin on these)**
- **Oklahoma:** effective around Jan 2027.
- **Louisiana:** effective around Jan 2027.
- **Alabama:** effective around May 2027.
- **Vermont:** effective Jan 1, 2028.

I don't have the official names for these four laws. The one source I found named them the "OKCDPA" for Oklahoma and the "ALDPA" for Alabama, and called Louisiana's "Act 502". That source also gave inconsistent totals (20 in effect plus 3 more, versus 24 overall).

**Caveats**
- Florida's law is much narrower than the others. It mainly covers companies with over $1 billion in revenue, so some trackers don't count it as comprehensive.
- Utah's law took effect on Dec 31, 2023, and some sources round that to Jan 1, 2024.

NHTSA lists five recalls for the 2020 Honda Civic:

| Campaign # | Component | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| 21V215000 | Fuel pump (in-tank, low-pressure) | The pump can fail and stall the engine while driving. This expands recall 20V-314. |
| 23V458000 | Service brakes: master cylinder | A tie rod fastener may have been assembled incorrectly. The master cylinder could separate from the booster and cause loss of braking. |
| 23V858000 | Fuel pump (in-tank) | The pump can fail and stall the engine while driving. This expands recalls 21V-215 and 20V-314. |
| 24V064000 | Air bags: front passenger occupant classification sensor | The seat weight sensor can crack and short-circuit, so the air bag may not be suppressed as intended. This is a phased recall. |

In 2025 Stripe shipped breaking changes in only three GA versions: `2025-03-31.basil`, `2025-09-30.clover`, and (on the preview channel only) a series of `.preview` versions. Stripe's model is that the first version of each named release carries all of that release's breaking changes, and later versions in the same release are additive. Every other 2025 GA version is non-breaking. That covers `2025-01-27.acacia`, `2025-02-24.acacia`, and `2025-04-30`, `2025-05-28`, `2025-06-30`, `2025-07-30` and `2025-08-27.basil`, plus `2025-10-29`, `2025-11-17` and `2025-12-15.clover`.

I took the lists below from Stripe's changelog tables. The one-line descriptions come from the entry titles. I did not open each entry's detail page, so check those before you plan a migration.

## GA versions

### 2025-03-31.basil (March 31, 2025)
This is the big one.

**Billing**
- Subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed. Billing periods now live on subscription items.
- Invoicing resources get a new `parent` field that says how they were generated.
- The Upcoming Invoice API methods are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
- Legacy usage-based billing is removed.
- Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items replace top-level price fields with a new price modeling.
- Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items replace top-level tax properties with a new tax modeling.
- Invoices support multiple (partial) payments.

**Coupons**
- Discount coupons with no specified end time are no longer supported.
- The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts.

**Checkout**
- Checkout Session shipping details are removed.
- Subscription Checkout Sessions now postpone creating the subscription until the customer pays. This also changes the update semantics and lowers latency.

**Payments**
- The Vault and Forward API returns 402 for upstream request timeouts.
- Manual capture is removed for Interac cards.
- Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after creation.
- Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.

**Issuing**
- There's a new reason code for authorizations created while Stripe is unavailable.
- Webhook `Accept` headers now specify JSON during Issuing authorizations.
- Authorizations get a new `expired` status.

**Connect**
- There are new error codes for required verifications.
- The Person object's political exposure property changes from a string to an enum.

**Platform and Stripe.js**
- You can no longer expand `total_count` on list methods.
- The default Payment Element layout changes (Stripe.js).

### 2025-09-30.clover (September 30, 2025)
**Billing**
- The `iterations` parameter is removed from subscription schedules.
- Promotion Codes reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
- Discounts gain a `source` property and lose the `coupon` property.
- Flexible billing mode becomes the default for new subscriptions.
- Subscription schedule phase end dates now take billing cycle anchor changes into account.

**Checkout and Stripe.js**
- Postal code collection is removed for card payments in certain regions on Checkout and Payment Element.
- The currency conversion field is removed from Checkout Sessions.
- `redirectToCheckout` is removed.
- `initCheckout` becomes synchronous.

**Elements (Stripe.js)**
- The default behavior for saved payment methods changes with Checkout Sessions.
- Client secrets for Intents in certain states can no longer be reused when initializing Elements.
- Deprecated messaging and bank elements that were replaced are removed.

**Connect**
- There are more specific descriptions for risk requirements during legal, PEP and sanctions review.
- There's a new error code for business type validation.

**Payments**
- The decline codes change for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and the South Korean payment methods.
- Submitted stablecoin payments get a `processing` status.

**Radar and Issuing**
- Radar manual reviews get additional enum values.
- Issuing Authorization risk levels switch to standard values.

## Preview-channel versions
These are in the public-preview channel and are not GA. They only matter if you've pinned a `.preview` version.

| Version | Date | Breaking changes |
|---|---|---|
| `2025-04-30.preview` | Apr 30 | Payouts become a capability in Accounts v2. |
| `2025-05-28.preview` | May 28 | Tax association status fields are replaced. The Payment Intent field that links a tax calculation is renamed. |
| `2025-06-30.preview` | Jun 30 | Billing mode configuration is consolidated into a single hash. |
| `2025-07-30.preview` | Jul 30 | Account Links v2 is enabled for Accounts v2. The Balance Settings custom settlement timing parameter is renamed. Weekly and monthly payout schedule customization is updated. A new Radar review close reason is added. |
| `2025-08-27.preview` | Aug 27 | Flexible billing mode becomes the default, which is the same change that went GA in Clover. Subscription schedule `iterations` is removed, same as Clover. The Balance Settings request object is nested under `payments`. |
| `2025-09-30.preview` | Sep 30 | Billing meter aggregated usage data gets pagination and field updates. Platform-specific identity fields move to a default profile for Accounts. Smart Disputes recommended evidence is restructured. |
| `2025-10-29.preview` | Oct 29 | There's a new error code for missing verification data on connected accounts. Accounts v2 payment method billing details are used for Stripe Tax location. |
| `2025-11-17.preview` | Nov 17 | Accounts v2 requirements collection parameters are updated. A future-requirements field is added. Health alerts for events that fail to generate are added. Meter Usage Analytics supports filtering multiple tenants and dimension values. |
| `2025-12-15.preview` | Dec 15 | Accounts v2 always returns `responsibilities` when `defaults` is included. The `requested` field is removed from Accounts v2 capabilities hashes. Generic error types are added for Payout Methods. |

## Upgrading
If you're pinned before March 2025, the Basil jump is the larger one (subscription periods, invoice shape, tax and pricing fields, Upcoming Invoice). Moving from Basil to Clover mostly touches discounts and coupons, subscription schedules, Stripe.js, and the Checkout changes.

Two later breaking changes landed in early 2026: Treasury `flow` becomes nullable, and the error codes change for Outbound Setup Intents. They are outside your 2025 question, so I didn't dig into them.

Sources:
- [Stripe changelog: Acacia](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/acacia)
- [Stripe changelog: Basil](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil)
- [Stripe changelog: Clover](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover)
